tasks.title: Safe calculator
tasks.statement: Write calc(expr): parse the string with ast.parse(expr, mode="eval") and evaluate it recursively, allowing only numbers (int, float), unary + and -, and binary + - * / // % **. Anything else (calls, names, strings) raises ValueError. The OPS and UNARY tables are already provided.
tasks.hint: A recursive function over nodes: Constant gives the value, BinOp gives OPS[type(node.op)](...), UnaryOp gives UNARY[...](...), otherwise raise ValueError.

tasks.title: Settings from literals only
tasks.statement: Write parse_config(text): turn the string into a value with ast.literal_eval. If the string is not a literal (a call, an expression) or has a syntax error, raise ValueError("invalid setting").
tasks.hint: try: return ast.literal_eval(text) except (ValueError, SyntaxError): raise ValueError("invalid setting").

tasks.title: Which functions the code calls
tasks.statement: Write called_names(source): a sorted list of the names of functions called by plain name (print(...), foo(...)). Ignore method calls like obj.method(). Use ast.NodeVisitor and remember to walk into nested calls.
tasks.hint: In visit_Call: if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name): names.add(node.func.id); then self.generic_visit(node).

tasks.title: How many functions are defined
tasks.statement: Write count_functions(source): the number of function and method definitions (def and async def, including nested ones); lambdas are not counted.
tasks.hint: sum(isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) for n in ast.walk(tree)).

tasks.title: Which modules the code imports
tasks.statement: Write imported_modules(source): a sorted list of the top-level module names that the source imports (import a.b gives a, from c.d import e gives c). Skip relative imports (from . import x).
tasks.hint: ast.Import: node.names[i].name.split('.')[0]; ast.ImportFrom: if node.level == 0, use node.module.split('.')[0].

tasks.title: Renaming a variable
tasks.statement: Write rename_var(source, old, new): use ast.NodeTransformer to rename all uses of the name old (Name nodes and function parameters arg) and return the text via ast.unparse.
tasks.hint: visit_Name: if node.id == old: node.id = new; return node. For parameters use visit_arg: node.arg.

tasks.title: Folding constants in advance
tasks.statement: Write fold_constants(source): a NodeTransformer replaces binary operations +, - and * on two numeric constants with a single constant, including nested ones. Return the result via ast.unparse.
tasks.hint: In visit_BinOp first call self.generic_visit(node); if left and right are ast.Constant and op is Add/Sub/Mult, compute the value and return ast.Constant(value).

tasks.title: exec in its own namespace
tasks.statement: Write build(source, name): run the source with exec in a new empty dictionary and return the object called name from it. The global names of your program must not change; if the name is missing, raise KeyError.

tasks.title: Calls and loops in bytecode
tasks.statement: Write count_calls(func), the number of call instructions (CALL, CALL_KW, CALL_FUNCTION_EX) in the function's bytecode, and has_loop(func), which reports whether there is a FOR_ITER instruction. Use dis.get_instructions.
tasks.hint: ops = [i.opname for i in dis.get_instructions(func)]; count the elements that belong to the set {"CALL", "CALL_KW", "CALL_FUNCTION_EX"}.
